name: Typo
description: One letter in the page heading changed: "Overview" became "Overwiew". A real regression that is only a few dozen pixels big.
lookFor: A tight threshold keeps it; a loose one, or a hash, calls the pages the same.

name: Button color
description: The primary button and the selected payment method drifted by three RGB points per channel (#4f46e5 → #4c49e2), the trace a changed design token leaves.
lookFor: Exact pixels and Resemble.js (ignore: nothing) flag every button pixel; pixelmatch at its default threshold, Resemble.js with ignore: less and SSIM let it pass. Lower the pixelmatch threshold to 0 to catch it.

name: Layout shift
description: The second stat card moved down by 4 px. Nothing inside it changed.
lookFor: Pixel engines paint the card edges and its text twice (old and new position); SSIM stays near 1 because the structure is the same, only moved. The blink view shows the move at once.

name: Anti-aliasing
description: The content was nudged by 0.3 px. Boxes snap back to the same pixels, but every glyph is rasterized at a new sub-pixel offset: pure rendering noise.
lookFor: pixelmatch with anti-aliasing detection (includeAA off) and Resemble.js with ignore: antialiasing drop most of it; turn includeAA on to see the noise counted.

name: Dynamic content
description: The clock advanced a minute, the online counter moved, and a different user is signed in (avatar and name). Content that changes on every run.
lookFor: Every engine reports it, correctly: these pixels did change. The fix is a mask over the dynamic regions in your tool, not a looser threshold.

name: Dark mode
description: The same page rendered with the dark theme. Almost every pixel differs.
lookFor: Pixel mismatch near 100%, an SSIM near 0, and even the perceptual hash, blind to small changes, has most of its bits flipped.

name: JPEG compression
description: The actual image is the same page saved as a JPEG at quality 60 and read back. No real change, but almost no pixel survives the codec untouched.
lookFor: Exact pixels and Resemble.js report most of the image; pixelmatch at threshold 0 does too. SSIM stays close to 1 because the structure is intact. Look at the gradient and the serif text for the artifacts.

name: Missing section
description: The "Notifications" section is gone, so everything below it moved up and the full-page screenshot got shorter: the two images have different sizes.
lookFor: pixelmatch and SSIM refuse different sizes on their own; the tool pads the shorter image so they can run. Resemble.js reports isSameDimensions: false.
